smud:cc-tod-5-8pm-2026-01-01: This filing carries the January 1, 2026 column of the RT02 rate: a $27.00 System Infrastructure Fixed Charge and five time-of-day usage prices. Four charges that Rate Schedule R-TOD also provides for are not represented. Section IV.D Standby Service Option, $8.855 per kW of Contract Capacity per month effective January 1, 2026, for customers whose on-site generation has a combined nameplate rating under 100 kW and is connected to SMUD's system, waived only for qualifying renewable generation under Schedules NEM1 and SSR. Section IV.H Residential Three-Phase Service Option, a Special Facilities fee of $57.95 per month effective January 1, 2026, billed in addition to the System Infrastructure Fixed Charge. Section III.A Hydro Generation Adjustment, a surcharge on all kWh set by a separate Rate Schedule HGA that this corpus does not carry. Section IV.F SMUD Renewable Energy Option, a voluntary renewable-energy charge for which the schedule states no amount, publishing it on smud.org instead. Two further gaps are in what is modeled rather than in what is absent. Section V.A gives eleven named holidays Off-Peak pricing, and this filing approximates that with weekday and weekend day types alone, attaching no holiday calendar, so a holiday falling on a weekday, such as Labor Day, resolves to Peak or Mid-Peak pricing rather than the Off-Peak the schedule directs. Section VI.A prorates the monthly System Infrastructure Fixed Charge against 30 days when the billing period is shorter than 27 days; the charge is carried here as a flat monthly amount with no proration rule (the usage charge, per the same section, is never prorated and so needs none). Section IV.G Special Metering Charge is out of scope rather than missing: it is a monthly service fee for nonstandard customer-purchased data-collection equipment billed under Rule and Regulation 2 Section IV, and the schedule publishes no amount for it. Finally, the Section I applicability limits, which exclude master-metered multifamily and mobile home park service and mandate R-TOD for customers whose NEM1 or SSR generation was approved on or after January 1, 2018, are carried in the eligibility rule's prose rather than as condition operands; the condition expression tests only that the customer is residential.
smud:cc-tod-low-use-2026-01-01: This filing carries the RTL1 prices of the January 1, 2026 column, a $17.00 System Infrastructure Fixed Charge and five time-of-day usage prices, and shares the unrepresented provisions of the Rate Schedule R-TOD document it is taken from. Section IV.D Standby Service Option, $8.855 per kW of Contract Capacity per month effective January 1, 2026, for customers whose on-site generation has a combined nameplate rating under 100 kW, waived only for qualifying renewable generation under Schedules NEM1 and SSR. Section IV.H Residential Three-Phase Service Option, $57.95 per month in Special Facilities fees effective January 1, 2026, in addition to the System Infrastructure Fixed Charge. Section III.A Hydro Generation Adjustment, a surcharge on all kWh under a separate Rate Schedule HGA not carried in this corpus. Section IV.F SMUD Renewable Energy Option, whose charge the schedule does not state, publishing it on smud.org. Two gaps sit inside what is modeled: the eleven holidays that Section V.A prices as Off-Peak are approximated with weekday and weekend day types and no holiday calendar, so a holiday falling on a weekday, such as Labor Day, resolves to Peak or Mid-Peak; and the Section VI.A proration of the monthly System Infrastructure Fixed Charge against 30 days for billing periods shorter than 27 days has no representation, the charge being carried as a flat monthly amount. Eligibility is the place where this rate differs from its RT02 sibling, and it is the weakest part of the model: Section I.B makes a service panel of 125 amps or less a hard requirement, and that requirement is stated in prose while the condition expression tests only that the customer is residential. The eligibility rule's own prose describes the rate election as an encoded predicate, but no such operand is present in the graph: nothing in the condition expression distinguishes an RTL1 customer from any other residential customer. The schedule's other qualifier, that the rate is for customers who 'use a low amount energy,' is left unquantified in the source, so nothing is modeled from it. Section IV.G Special Metering Charge is out of scope rather than missing: it is a service fee for nonstandard customer-purchased metering equipment, billed under Rule and Regulation 2 Section IV, and carries no published amount.
smud:cc-cpp-2026-01-01: This filing carries the three price components the CPP rate overlays on its Time-of-Day base plan: the Event Price of $0.5000 per kWh and the summer Mid-Peak and Off-Peak discounts of $0.0200 per kWh each. What is not represented is the machinery around them. Section I.C.3 limits Events to between one and four hours, not more than one per day, callable in any hour of a summer day including weekends and holidays, up to 50 hours per summer, and Section I.C.4 requires a day-ahead announcement except in a system emergency; the only structural gate this filing puts on the Event Price is that the month be June through September, with the rest of the trigger carried as prose on a price update rule, so nothing in the graph distinguishes an Event hour from an ordinary summer hour and a consumer must apply SMUD's event calendar itself. Section II.C.4 compensates energy exported to the grid during an Event at the same Event Price; the charge here is modeled in the consuming direction only, with the export side left in prose. Section I.C.2's cap of 30,000 enrolled customers and Section I.C.1's mandatory enrollment for customers who have accepted a storage incentive under certain SMUD Solar and Storage incentive programs both sit in the eligibility rule's description; its condition expression tests only that the customer is residential and carries a free-text 'Program Enrollment' of 'CPP'. That free-text predicate is itself forced: URPX's list of program types is closed and has no value for critical peak pricing, so no typed program enrollment can be attached. One provision is outside the tariff document rather than missing from the model: Section II.C.5 puts the Event Price and the discount on smud.org, updated annually at SMUD's discretion, so the values here are those posted at the retrieval date and each annual update needs a new version.
smud:cc-fixed-2026-01-01: Rate Schedule R publishes two rate categories and this filing models one. The Fixed Rate (RF01) is complete for the January 1, 2026 column: a $27.00 System Infrastructure Fixed Charge per meter per month and flat usage charges of $0.2189 per kWh in summer and $0.1371 per kWh in the non-summer season. Sections I.C and II.B of the same schedule carry Master-Metered Multifamily Accommodation and Mobile Home Park Billing (rate category RSMM), closed to new customers but still served, with its own published prices of $27.00 per unit per month, $0.1740 per kWh in summer and $0.1520 per kWh in the non-summer season, and its own billing method under which consumption is the master meter's total kWh divided by the number of occupied single-family accommodations. None of that is modeled. Four charges the schedule provides for are also absent: Section IV.E Standby Service Option at $8.855 per kW of Contract Capacity per month effective January 1, 2026, for on-site generation under 100 kW combined nameplate and waived only for qualifying renewable generation under Schedules NEM1 and SSR; Section IV.J Residential Three-Phase Service Option at $57.95 per month in Special Facilities fees effective January 1, 2026; Section III.A Hydro Generation Adjustment, a surcharge on all kWh set by a separate Rate Schedule HGA that this corpus does not carry; and Section IV.G SMUD Renewable Energy Option, for which the schedule states no amount, publishing it on smud.org. The Section V proration table is likewise unrepresented: the fixed charge is carried as a flat monthly amount, where the schedule prorates it against 30 days when the billing period is shorter than 27 days and prorates kWh both for that case and for periods longer than 34 days. Section IV.H Special Metering Charge is out of scope rather than missing, being a monthly service fee for nonstandard customer-purchased data-collection equipment billed under Rule and Regulation 2 Section IV with no amount published in the tariff. One weakness is worth naming: the Section I.A rules that decide who may take the Fixed Rate at all, which bar customers with NEM1 generation approved on or after January 1, 2018, any SSR generation, storage without an associated generating facility, or a master meter on RSMM, are described in the eligibility rule's prose while its condition expression tests only that the customer is residential.
smud:cc-eapr-2023-09-22: Schedule EAPR grants residential customers two discounts and this filing models the smaller one. Section III.1, a $10 per month System Infrastructure Fixed Charge discount, is represented. Section III.2 is not: a 100 percent reduction in electricity usage cost per kWh up to a monthly maximum that steps with the household's federal poverty level, $60 at 0 to 50 percent, $32 above 50 to 100 percent, $10 above 100 to 150 percent and $0 above 150 to 200 percent. Nor is Section III.3, the EAPR Rate Stabilization Fund discount, a further $0 to $35 per month available only at 0 to 50 percent of the federal poverty level, its amount set each year by SMUD's Accountant from whatever discretionary non-retail revenue is available and fixed before the year it applies. The effect on a consumer depends entirely on which income tier a customer sits in: between 150 and 200 percent of the federal poverty level the usage cap is $0 and the modeled $10 is the whole benefit, while at 0 to 50 percent the two unmodeled components are worth up to $95 a month more than what this filing carries. Section VIII is also unrepresented: the fixed-charge discount is prorated against 30 days for billing periods shorter than 27 days, while the maximum usage discount is expressly not prorated. Sections IV and V are out of scope rather than missing. They cover nonprofit organizations and Commercial and Industrial customers: the nonprofit eligibility tests, including the requirement that at least 75 percent of an associated daytime-services facility's square footage serve the qualifying functions, and the Commercial and Industrial discounts of 15 percent on usage, maximum demand, site infrastructure and summer peak demand charges with a 35 percent System Infrastructure Fixed Charge discount on CI-TOD1 and 15 percent on CI-TOD2 through CI-TOD4. This filing is scoped to residential service.
smud:cc-med-2017-07-01: Schedule MED grants a single benefit, a $15.00 per month discount applied to the electricity usage portion of the bill, and this filing carries it, but not at the granularity the schedule states. It is modeled as a per-day credit of $0.4931, being $15.00 divided by an average month of 30.4 days, so it reproduces the stated amount only for a billing period of exactly that length. SMUD's residential schedules define a month as a billing period of 27 to 34 days, which puts the modeled credit between roughly $13.31 and $16.77 against a schedule amount that does not vary with the length of the period. The credit is also carried as a flat per-meter amount rather than one scoped to the electricity usage portion of the bill, which is where Section II places it. Section III, under which a customer qualified for both this program and the Energy Assistance Program Rate receives both discounts, is stated in this filing's prose but not as a structured relationship to the EAPR modifier. The Section IV conditions are out of scope rather than missing: the application and the certification by a qualified health professional, the definition of that term and the list of qualifying devices and medical conditions that SMUD maintains on its website rather than in the schedule, and the Section IV.C invitation to contact SMUD when the discount does not meet a household's needs are enrollment and customer-service procedures rather than rate components, as are the Section V rules fixing when enrollment and cancellation take effect.
smud:cc-nem1-2021-09-17: The compensation this schedule grants is the part the filing cannot state. Section V.D credits excess exported electricity at retail value, meaning the energy charge of whichever base rate the customer is on, and allows those credits only against electricity usage charges. A URPX price reference has to point at a price typed in the same document, and the base rate here is the customer's own R-TOD or Fixed Rate plan rather than anything this filing contains, so it ships a placeholder price of zero: read the credit from the customer's base plan, not from the zero carried here. The limit is recorded upstream at urpx-org/urpx discussion 34. The settlement mechanics of Section VI are unmodeled as well: a 12-month settlement period over which monthly credits carry forward, with unused accumulated credit liable to be zeroed out at the end of it. So is the Section VI.A annual net surplus election, under which a customer with net surplus over the 12 months takes either a monetary payment or a roll-over of the surplus kWh, the payment rate being set from the most recent SMUD budget as expected avoided generation and production-related costs divided by forecasted annual energy sales and published on smud.org by December 20 before the year it applies, with the renewable energy credits for purchased kWh passing to SMUD; the schedule states no dollar figure, so none is carried. Section VI.B's opt-out, under which a customer forgoes all surplus compensation and keeps the associated renewable energy credits, is absent too. Section II exempts these customers from generator standby charges on the portion of load served by the eligible facility, and that exemption has nothing to attach to because the Standby Service Charge of Schedules R and R-TOD is itself not modeled in this corpus. Four eligibility conditions are structural: residential service, the Section I requirement that the interconnection application was approved before March 1, 2022, a qualifying renewable generation type, and the 3,000 kW capacity ceiling of Section III.A.9. The other eight requirements of Section III.A are prose only, among them parallel operation with SMUD's distribution facilities, compliance with Rule and Regulation 21, a single metering point, the facility being intended primarily to offset the customer's own use, the disqualification of customers who have taken SMUD storage incentives, and the ceiling on growth above originally approved capacity of 10 percent or 1 kW, whichever is greater, and 110 percent in total. Section VII, which requires residential customers whose facility was approved on or after January 1, 2018 to be on Rate Schedule R-TOD, is prose as well. Two decisions are scope rather than gap: the schedule also covers commercial, industrial and agricultural customers and this filing is residential only, and the Section IV bidirectional meter SMUD installs at no cost is a metering operation rather than a rate.
